chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Hadeed ibn Hakeem or Murazam, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Any believer who conveys a kindness to his believing brother, has thereby conveyed it to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.أَخِيهِ: his brother (referring to a fellow believer)
key_terms.أَوْصَلَ: to convey, to connect, to bring about
key_terms.مَعْرُوفاً: an act of kindness, goodness, or benevolence

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for showing kindness to another believer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (as) establishes a spiritual chain of attribution, where kindness between believers is directly credited to the Prophet Muhammad (saww), emphasizing the concept of *tawassul* through social bonds. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that the community of believers constitutes an extension of the Prophet’s presence, making interpersonal piety a direct form of devotion to him. The narration underscores that maintaining ties of kinship and friendship is not merely a social duty but a sacred act that carries the weight of prophetic merit.
